67.t: Roy Hargrove and the young trumpet players
67.s: Cheatham follows Roy Hargrove and compares today's players, who hear more, with his own self-made path.
67.q: Yes, I’m very interested in that. I hear a lot of these kids today and I’m surprised to hear what they’re playing. They’re playing so, so pretty and so beautiful, and I wonder where it’s coming from. And now I see where it’s coming from. I follow Roy Hargrove, because he’s such a nice guy — a lot…

67.t: Admiring young trumpeters Warren Vache and Jon Faddis
67.s: He likes Vache for sitting in with older players and thinks Faddis has the will to reach the top.
67.q: -- I like him very much. Cause he's doing the things -- he did the things that we used to do. He goes around and sits in with all of us. He comes over -- he came over where I played in Jersey, almost every week and bring his horn and get on the bandstand and we jammed together, we played together.

1014.t: Closing remembrances: idol, angels and the future of traditional jazz
1014.s: She calls him the most wonderful person she met, his playing like talking with angels, and says he wished more young players followed traditional jazz.
1014.q: Oh, not really, Tom. All I can think of is that he's the most wonderful person I've ever met. I mean, his playing to me naturally will always be the greatest thing. He's always been my idol since I've been a child. And for me to come in contact, as I had with him, with an idol, which was like some…

676.t: Jazz today and the loss of Herschel Evans
676.s: Today's players have chops but stand on earlier musicians' shoulders; she wishes she could hear Herschel Evans.
676.q: Gee I don’t know. I have people I always go and see — Ahmad Jamal, I’m crazy about him. I would like to hear some big bands occasionally. Gosh, Jimmy Heath came by the table yesterday at the Life thing and said that he has a big band playing at the Iridium Room. I thought he said it was just last…

101.t: Roy Hargrove and the younger trumpeters
101.s: Praise for Roy Hargrove, whom Terry helped through Berklee, and for Nicholas Payton.
101.q: Well you know he’s a very special kid to me because my wife Gwen knows his mother very well. And she headed up a program called STAR, Students Targeting Adult Responsibility. And they were basically responsible for his education. They’ve gotten funds from different sources, now even I kicked in a…

651.t: Notable camp alumni and what the camp gives young players
651.s: Chris Potter, Pat Metheny, Mulgrew Miller, James Williams and others attended, and meeting faculty helped careers.
651.q: Steve Rodby. Mulgrew Miller. James Williams. Chris Botti. And a couple of more. There’s a list of about 20 who have come to the camp at one time or another, probably one time, but it helped them make... As a matter of fact, I’ve thought about this often. Somebody comes to the camp and they’re…

589.t: Younger pianists today: Jason Moran, Danilo Perez, Rubalcaba
589.s: Lewis names younger pianists he likes and says they need polish and experience as they mature.
589.q: That’s what I mean. When these younger ones get as old as Danilo and Rubalcaba, they’re going to be even better. I like them, even now, but I can hear youthful things that need a little polishing here, a little polishing there. When you’re young, sometimes it’s “Ma, look, no hands.” I think you…

104.t: Promising young artists: Benny Green and Geoff Keezer
104.s: She names Benny Green, whom she first heard with Art Blakey, and Geoff Keezer as young artists developing well.
104.q: God . . . I would have to say Benny Green of course. Somebody told me about him when he was with Art [Blakey]. I was in California, and I went to Catalina’s Restaurant, because Art was there, just to hear Benny Green. He looked like a kid. He still looks like a kid. He had a high collar on. He…

114.s: He names Terence Blanchard, Antonio Hart and David Sanchez as promising younger players.
114.q: Oh. Blanchet (phonetic sp.), Antonio Heart (phonetic sp.), little -- what's the guys name, honey, the little kid in Telluride? His mother and father live here? LINDA: Brian Lent (phonetic sp.).

367.s: Young praises young trumpeters in the Clayton-Hamilton band and Winston Bird, and hopes another Louis or Roy comes along.
367.q: He‘s a good young trumpet player. He‘s got chops [shoo]. These cats, I don‘t know where they get these chops from now-a-days. There must be something different about these chops because they all whistling up there, I say, ―Wow.‖ I like some of the young trumpet players. And I can, I tell when they…

92.s: Hubbard's trumpet reminds Collins of Rex Stewart, another reason young players should go back and listen.
92.ch: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
92.q: Yeah. I heard the trumpet players now doing Freddy Hubbard and a lot of the things that he does reminds me of Rex Stewart. You see, Rex Stewart was a great trumpet player, he was an innovator, you know, and a lot of the things that the trumpet players are doing now, and especially Freddy Hubbard,…

235.t: Younger players he likes and hearing Dexter Gordon at the Vanguard
235.s: He praises John Hicks, Walter Booker and Ricky Ford, and recalls an evening with Dexter Gordon at the Vanguard and hearing Slide Hampton.
235.q: : Well John Hicks and Walter Booker, because they have the right mental attitude. And I heard this little young tenor player, Ricky Ford; he has the right mental attitude. And, well you know that I was so busy since I been here that I haven't had really a chance to get around to hear, you know, a…

611.t: How Driver recommended him, and a young pianist today
611.s: Driver told Miller about him, the way word gets around; this prompts an aside about a fine young pianist Waters recently worked with.
611.q: Like I told you about the drummer here that I worked with, little piano player I'm gonna sit - well, I think it's fine, well, that's the way the news gets around finally. He gets a job through that way.
